newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ to continue current asset sale position - Bolger.
newsitem.headline: NZ to continue current asset sale position - Bolger.

text.p: New Zealand Prime Minister Jim Bolger said on Wednesday the new coalition government will continue along the same vein in its approach to asset sales.
He ruled out the privatisation of state generator Electricity Corporation of New Zealand, national grid operator Trans Power or New Zealand Post.
Bolger was speaking shortly after his caretaker conservative National Party signed a coalition deal with the nationalist New Zealand First Party.

He said the deal did not include any buy-back of former state-owned enterprise Forestry Corporation, which was sold for NZ$2 billion in September to a consortium of Fletcher Challenge Forest Division, Brierley Investments Ltd and China's Citic.
New Zealand First had campaigned for October's election on a promise to buy back Forestry Corp.
The coalition deal, announced on Tuesday night, ended nearly two months of political suspense over powerbroker NZ First's choice of partner between National and Labour.
